email_body:
Dear itsme team,

I'm applying for the Content Creator role. For the past few years I've worked where SEO, content and web meet: writing SEO articles and web copy, publishing in WordPress and Shopify, and building sites from structure to launch. At Episto I write and publish client content and run keyword research; freelance, I built mirook.com from sitemap to schema, turning technical detail into pages people actually read.

English is where I write to publication standard today, and I'm actively raising my Dutch — writing at B1, speaking A2+, improving every week.

The part of the job I'd enjoy most is getting your busy experts to say the useful thing out loud, then writing it down better than they said it. I'd welcome a conversation.

cover_letter:
Dear hiring team,

I'd like to be the person who turns what your experts know into what your B2B audience actually wants to read.

I work where SEO, content and web meet. At Episto I run keyword research, on-page SEO and the content itself for client sites — consultancy, e-commerce, a pharmacists' association where I keep roughly 600 member pages consistent — and I publish all of it in WordPress. Freelance, I built mirook.com from structure to schema: JSON-LD for Person, SportsEvent and FAQPage, entity and knowledge-graph markup, an llms.txt file, and iterative audits that measurably raised the site's search health. That work, plus the Semrush SEO certifications I hold, is built for the shift towards AI answer engines the posting mentions.

Getting the useful thing out of busy people is familiar ground. At Knowledge Experts I supported SharePoint-based digital workplace builds for ŞOK Market and Aras Kargo, where understanding what technical and business colleagues needed and turning it into structure and copy was most of the job. That is the same loop as your interview-and-write process.

I build the page, not just the text: a hand-coded landing page with a WebGL hero for baverok.com, Canva for visuals, HTML and CSS when a layout needs to behave. I hold a HubSpot Content Marketing certification, which is where my interest in HubSpot CMS comes from, and I read GA4 and Search Console to see what earns attention.

One thing I'd rather say up front: my Dutch writing is at B1 and my speaking at A2+, so the Dutch-first market is something I would grow into quickly rather than arrive in fully formed. English is where I write to publication standard today, and living in Zwijndrecht means daily practice comes free.

Your Curiosity and Humble values describe how I work: dig until it is clear, then take the edit.

Baver Ok
cv_highlights:
• Writes and publishes SEO content end to end: keyword research, on-page SEO, blog and web copy, published in WordPress and Shopify for client sites including a professional association with roughly 600 member pages
• Turns one piece into everything that follows it: structured data, landing pages, schema and internal linking, built with search intent and AI answer engines in mind (GEO/AEO, llms.txt)
• Interviews experts and translates them: supported SharePoint digital workplace builds for ŞOK Market (4,000+ stores) and Aras Kargo (12,000 staff), turning what technical and business colleagues know into structure and copy
• Works across markets and languages: English fluent to publication standard, Dutch writing B1 and improving, Turkish native; based in Zwijndrecht, Belgium
• Ships the visual and technical side too: Canva, hand-coded landing page with a WebGL hero, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Python automation, HubSpot Content Marketing and Semrush SEO certifications, GA4 and Google Search Console
